mlTraining.label: ML Training
mlTraining.title: Model Training Lab
mlTraining.description: Train ML models with alpha-zoo factors, walk-forward CV, and anti-leakage auditing. Compare models and deploy signals to backtesting.

models.empty: No trained models yet. Go to the Train tab to create one.

train.overfitWarning: Overfit detected: train/test IC ratio exceeds 3×. Consider reducing model complexity or increasing regularization.

tips.models: This table shows all trained models. IC (Information Coefficient) measures prediction quality; AUC measures classification accuracy. An overfit warning means the model memorizes training data instead of learning patterns.
tips.train: Configure and launch model training. Walk-forward CV trains on historical data and tests on future data — mimicking real trading. Purge+Embargo automatically prevent label leakage at fold boundaries.
tips.features: Feature Profiles decouple feature selection from model training. Create a profile once, reuse it across multiple models. Use an earlier time period for selection to prevent selection bias leaking into training.
tips.compare: Select 2+ models to compare CV metrics side by side. Look for consistent IC across folds (low overfit ratio) rather than the highest single IC. Same horizon models are most comparable.
tips.health: Check if deployed models are decaying. Drift score = (train_IC - recent_IC) / train_IC. Score > 0.5 means the model has lost >50% of its predictive power and should be retrained.

overview.title: How ML Training Works
overview.p1: The ML Training module turns Alpha Zoo factors into predictive trading signals. It follows a strict pipeline designed to prevent look-ahead bias (data leakage) at every step.

step1.title: Feature Engineering
step1.desc: Compute alpha-zoo factors (up to 452) as features. Optionally filter via IC, correlation, SHAP, or Boruta to keep only predictive factors.

step2.title: Model Training
step2.desc: Train LightGBM, XGBoost, Ridge, or Deep NN with walk-forward cross-validation. Purge+Embargo prevent label leakage. Overfit detection warns when train/test gap is too large.

step3.title: Compare & Ensemble
step3.desc: Compare models by IC, AUC, Sharpe, and backtest metrics. Combine top models into an ensemble (average, IC-weighted, or stacking) for more robust signals.

step4.title: Deploy & Monitor
step4.desc: Use the best model in backtesting via mf_ml_predictor strategy. Monitor for alpha decay and set up sliding-window retraining schedules.

quickstart.title: Quick Start (5 Steps)
quickstart.s1: Go to the Features tab and create a Feature Profile. Use a period before your training period (e.g. 2018-2020 for selection, 2020-2024 for training).
quickstart.s2: Go to the Train tab. Select your universe, training period, model type, and label config. Set the feature_profile_id to the profile you just created.
quickstart.s2code: Universe: CSI 300 | Period: 2020-2024 | Model: LightGBM | Horizon: 5d | Label: binary
quickstart.s3: Repeat Step 2 with different models (XGBoost, Ridge) or horizons (1d, 7d, 14d) to create multiple models for comparison.
quickstart.s4: Go to the Compare tab. Select all your models and click Compare. Look for the model with the best IC and lowest overfit ratio.
quickstart.s5: Use the winning model_id in a backtest: set strategy to mf_ml_predictor and pass the model_id as a parameter. Or create an ensemble from the top models for more stable signals.

leakage.title: Anti-Leakage Protection (6 Layers)
leakage.intro: Look-ahead bias is the #1 cause of backtesting results that don't hold in production. The training pipeline enforces 6 layers of protection, and every training run is audited automatically.

purge.name: Label Purge
purge.desc: Removes training samples whose forward-return labels extend into the test period. Purge window = label horizon (e.g. 5 days for 5-day returns).

embargo.name: Embargo Gap
embargo.desc: Additional buffer days between purged training data and test data to break autocorrelation leakage.

selectionLeak.name: Selection Bias Guard
selectionLeak.desc: Feature selection runs on a separate time period (Mode A) or within each CV fold (Mode B). Never on the full dataset.

preprocessLeak.name: Preprocessing Guard
preprocessLeak.desc: Winsorize quantiles and z-score parameters are computed only on training-fold data, then applied to test data. Never fitted on test data.

survivorship.name: Survivorship Bias Check
survivorship.desc: Point-in-time constituent loading ensures each historical date uses that date's actual index members, including stocks that were later delisted.

cacheLeak.name: Cache Integrity
cacheLeak.desc: Feature cache only appends new dates forward. No backfilling. Preprocessing parameters are never cached — they're recomputed per training fold.

features.title: Feature Selection Methods
features.intro: 452 raw factors contain noise and redundancy. Feature selection keeps only the factors that genuinely predict returns, improving model quality and preventing overfitting.

methods.ic_filter: Keep factors with |ICIR| above threshold (default 0.3). Spearman rank IC measures monotonic prediction power.
methods.corr_dedup: Among highly correlated factor pairs (|corr| > 0.85), keep the one with higher IC. Removes redundant information.
methods.mutual_info: Mutual Information score captures non-linear dependencies between factors and returns. Catches patterns IC misses.
methods.shap: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) measures each factor's contribution to model predictions, considering interactions.
methods.boruta: Creates shadow features (randomly shuffled copies), trains Random Forest, statistically tests which real features outperform shadows.
methods.importance: Uses a trained model's gain-based feature importance to prune factors contributing < 1% of total gain.

models.title: Supported Models
models.intro: Four model backends are available. LightGBM and XGBoost handle missing values natively and are recommended for most use cases. Ridge is always available as a baseline.

lightgbm.name: LightGBM
lightgbm.desc: Gradient boosting with leaf-wise growth. Fast training, strong tabular performance. Default: 63 leaves, lr=0.05, 500 trees.

xgboost.name: XGBoost
xgboost.desc: Gradient boosting with level-wise growth. Mature, well-tuned. Default: depth=6, lr=0.05, 500 trees.

ridge.name: Ridge Regression
ridge.desc: L2-regularized linear regression. Always available as a baseline — if it beats tree models, your features are too noisy.

deep_nn.name: Deep Neural Network
deep_nn.desc: 3-layer MLP (256→128→1) with BatchNorm and Dropout. For capturing non-linear factor interactions.

labels.title: Label Types & Configuration
labels.intro: Labels define what the model learns to predict. Different label types suit different trading strategies and model types.

return.usage: Regression models, continuous signal strength ranking

rank.usage: Regression models, when absolute return scale varies across time

binary.usage: Classification models (LightGBM/XGBoost auto-detect), clear buy/no-buy signal

top_bottom.usage: Long-short strategies, models trained only on extreme outcomes

labels.benchmark: Benchmark: Set to an index code (e.g. 000300.SH) to predict excess returns (alpha) instead of absolute returns. The model learns stock-picking skill, not market beta.
labels.cost: Transaction Cost: Set cost_bps (e.g. 15 = 15 basis points round-trip) to deduct trading costs before labeling. Prevents the model from learning "signals" that don't survive transaction costs.

lifecycle.title: Model Lifecycle & Production
lifecycle.intro: After finding a good model, deploy it and keep it healthy over time.

ensemble.name: Ensemble
ensemble.desc: Combine 2+ models via averaging, IC-weighting, or stacking. Ensembles typically outperform any single model by reducing variance.

sliding.name: Sliding-Window Retraining
sliding.desc: Set a schedule (monthly, quarterly) to automatically retrain with a rolling data window. Keeps the model adapted to recent market conditions.

health.name: Health Monitoring
health.desc: Regularly compare recent OOS IC with training CV IC. Drift score > 0.5 means the model has decayed significantly — retrain or replace.

promote.name: Version Management
promote.desc: Each retrain creates a new version. Promote the best version to 'production'. The signal engine auto-uses the promoted version.
